boundary: The agent may guide the approved self-service flow only; it must not reset credentials itself.
Ordinary lockouts are not agent-resolvable because identity verification and unlock require IAM.
MFA reset is specialist-led; never disable or bypass MFA to make sign-in work.

Agent can collect evidence and route; entitlement grants remain approval-controlled. Identity-provider or account-lifecycle entitlement faults belong to IAM; application-specific roles belong to Application Support. Use observed scope to select the owner.
Route to Application Support when evidence isolates the fault to one application.
No autonomous data-changing fix without an approved article and verified conditions.
Do not restart services automatically. Use outage workflow and human incident ownership.
No replay/reprocessing that may duplicate or alter records without specialist approval.
Never reactivate an account autonomously.
Do not delete other users' print jobs or change shared print-server configuration autonomously.
Cleanup must remain user-confirmed and limited to approved safe targets.
Never resolve or grant privileged access autonomously.
No autonomous unlock, password reset, or bypass.
Do not disable security controls or share VPN credentials.
No destructive device reset or software removal without specialist approval.
No autonomous gateway restart.
Never auto-delete, quarantine, or declare benign.
No changes to network security settings or shared credentials.
Do not change DNS records autonomously.
No autonomous restart or infrastructure configuration change.
Never run cleanup tools or instruct user to delete evidence.
Agent may provide approved guidance; resolve only after user confirms completion.
Never force a diagnosis or self-resolve with insufficient evidence.
Certificate changes require specialist and change-control approval.
Do not delete evidence or make disclosure/notification decisions autonomously.

Do not delete shared data or run destructive storage operations autonomously. Shared infrastructure/storage-layer faults belong to Infrastructure; application-isolated storage errors belong to Application Support. Use service-health and affected-scope evidence.
